# COR110 `nonportable-shortcircuit-inquiry`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A condition tests `present`/`allocated`/`associated` and uses the same entity in one expression.

## Why

Fortran does not short-circuit `.and.`/`.or.`: in `present(x) .and. x > 0` the compiler may evaluate
`x > 0` even when `x` is absent, which is invalid and crashes with some compilers and options.
Nest the tests (`if (present(x)) then; if (x > 0) ...`) or use a local copy set from the optional
argument.

## Reported

```fortran
if (present(tol) .and. tol > 0) eps = tol
```

## Preferred

```fortran
if (present(tol)) then
  if (tol > 0) eps = tol
end if
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR110] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR110` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C161` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
